questions.question: Which scope and order should stage three follow?

options.label: Process, 052, 055, 053 (Recommended)
options.description: PR1 BK-465+BK-466 only, small, first (keys session may need it). Then one dialog on the driver-duty home and 052's contradictions; PR2 prunes 052; PR3 creates the driver-interface spec as a pure move out of 053 (and 052's driver rows); PR4 prunes 053 minus the key clauses; 003 after, with BE-029 after spec 054. BK-467 left out: prose governs either way.

options.label: Your default as written
options.description: PR1 process; 052 prune; 053 prune with the driver-duty home decided in 053's dialog; 003 last. Risk: 052's BE-033 driver rows get placed before their home is chosen, and may move twice.

options.label: 053 first, then 052
options.description: Process PR, then 053 (minus key clauses), since BK-450 is due first and depends most on 053; 052 after. Larger first prune, and 053 shares more text with the keys session.

options.label: A-01 form, exempt (Recommended)
options.description: Template becomes <PREFIX>-A-01 (grammar unchanged); each spec gets its own prefix (003 BE-A-, 052 LIFE-A-, 053 KERN-A-), so no collision. check_spec_marks exempts -A-nn rows from the drift rule: citable, a stale citation still fails, a mark not required.

options.label: A-01 form, marked
options.description: Same IDs, but each assumption row is a shipped ID: a test must mark it or it goes on the allowlist. Strict, and most environment assumptions (OS atomicity, vendor thread-safety) would end up allowlisted.

options.label: Widen the grammar
options.description: Keep the template's <PREFIX>-A01; change _SPEC_ID in check_spec_marks.py and check_formal_trace.py to accept it. Touches two gates and every consumer of the ID shape.

options.label: Existing homes (Recommended)
options.description: Rule 1 drops "design note" and names the homes: rationale with alternatives to an ADR; how the kernel does it to the module docstring beside the code (changes with it); what a driver author must do to the custom-backend guide; enumerated cases to test docstrings. AUTHORING gains no type.

options.label: New sdd/design/ notes
options.description: Add a repo-only design-note type to AUTHORING (sdd/design/<subject>.md, e.g. the kernel pipeline and probe sequences). One durable place for mechanism, but a doc that drifts from code unless something checks it.

questions.question: Where do the driver duties live?

options.label: New spec 055 (Recommended)
options.description: A driver-interface spec: the driver's single-call duties from 053 (A.8's list, construction refusals, BE-031's primitives) and 003 BE-021's four driver rows, one home for BK-450. The driver's lifetime duties (idempotent close, abort after failed commit) stay in 052 as their own sections, by Rule 2. Revisits stage two's "does not split further".

options.label: One 053 section
options.description: A single "Driver duties" section in 053 holding every single-call duty; lifetime ones stay in 052. Fewer files, but 053 keeps two interfaces (audit W1).

options.label: Protocol docstrings only
options.description: Specs state only the kernel's observable outcomes; driver duties live on the driver protocols in src/remote_store/_kernel. BK-450 enforces from there. No spec states what a driver owes.
